title: Customer Communication And Product Feedback Checkpoint

questions.prompt: A sponsor adds scope without extending the date. What communication best supports a decision?

options.label: Send an unexplained refusal with no relation to the outcome.
Explain options, consequences and a recommendation with a decision owner.
Agree immediately and hide omitted testing.

questions.explanation: Visible tradeoffs make a decision possible. Concealed omissions and unexplained refusal prevent shared understanding.

questions.prompt: You do not know whether the customer API supports idempotency. What should you say?

options.label: State the uncertainty, identify how to verify it and avoid promising retry safety yet.
Promise exactly-once effects because most APIs probably support it.
Avoid mentioning the uncertainty until after deployment.

questions.explanation: A credible engineer distinguishes verified contracts from assumptions. Guessing or withholding an important uncertainty creates preventable delivery risk.

questions.prompt: The live integration fails during a demo and you switch to a synthetic recording. What must you disclose?

options.label: Nothing, as long as the video looks like the application.
Claim the recording proves current production recovery.
The fallback environment and what it does and does not demonstrate.

questions.explanation: A labeled fallback can preserve a useful discussion. It cannot establish the current integration state or recovery.

questions.prompt: Which field report is most actionable for the product team?

options.label: A vague request to make the platform better.
A safe minimal reproduction, versions, impact, workaround and evidence of recurrence.
A private customer data dump with no explanation.

questions.explanation: A reproducible report lets engineers investigate and prioritize. Sensitive dumps and vague feedback are neither sufficient nor appropriate evidence.
